extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in corporate crisis communication, argumentation and discourse studies, and public relations professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Critical-analysis of corporate crisis communication strategies (specifically strategic manoeuvring by dissociation) through case study of public statements and social media responses. Focuses on rhetorical/argumentative moves, stages of argumentation, audience demands, and institutional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dissociation as strategic manoeuvring
rubrics_metrics.description: United Airlines adopted dissociation using the lexical item 'volunteer' in the different stages of argumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper identifies dissociation (redefining or splitting a concept) as an explicit strategic manoeuvre; the lexical framing of 'volunteer' is the core example analyzed for how a corporation distances itself from responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application across stages of argumentation (bringing forward / maintaining / mitigating a standpoint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dissociation was used in the different stages of argumentation: bringing forward a standpoint, maintaining a standpoint and mitigating a standpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether and how dissociative moves appear at each argumentative stage — e.g., how the notion is introduced, defended, and softened — and the rhetorical functions they serve at those stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manipulation of topical potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The corporation strategically manoeuvred the topical potential ... to meet the demands of its primary audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the choice of topics, definitions, and focal points shapes what issues are considered relevant or off-topic for critical discussion (i.e., what the dissociation makes topical vs. untopic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of presentational devices
rubrics_metrics.description: The corporation strategically manoeuvred ... the presentational devices to meet the demands of its primary audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider visual/verbal presentation choices (wording, tone, emphasis, sequencing) and how they package the dissociation to influence audience interpretation and sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience orientation (meeting demands of the international general public)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic manoeuvring was intended to meet the demands of its primary audience, i.e. the international general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether rhetorical moves are tailored to the expectations, values, and information needs of the target audience, and how audience heterogeneity affects effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexical choice and definitional framing (e.g., 'volunteer')
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis focuses on the lexical item 'volunteer' as the vehicle for dissociation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine specific word choices and definitional framings that enable dissociation, including dictionary senses and pragmatic implications; small lexical shifts can reassign responsibility or change perceived facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment against general rules for critical discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The argumentative effectiveness was called into question based upon the general rules for critical discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge argumentative moves by standards from pragma-dialectics/critical discussion (e.g., clarity of standpoints, burden of proof, relevance, avoidance of fallacies) to see if the manoeuvres are dialectically acceptable or fallacious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of institutional context
rubrics_metrics.description: Argumentative effectiveness was called into question ... based upon ... the institutional context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for organizational constraints, legal/regulatory frameworks, and institutional reputational considerations that shape what communications are possible or persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel selection and public statement sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The study analysed public statements issued on its official website and Twitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include channel-appropriate criteria: differences in affordances, audience reach, tone expectations, and temporal dynamics between official website posts and social media replies; assess timing and platform choice as part of strategic manoeuvring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing corporate interest with argumentative legitimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Employing dissociation ... seemed to be reasonable and served the corporation’s interests best, [but] its argumentative effectiveness was called into question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tension between moves that protect corporate interests (damage control, legal exposure mitigation) and those that satisfy norms of reasonable argumentation and public acceptability; identify trade-offs and potential reputational costs.
